utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Case Number IT-03-67-PT, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I welcome you all. But before we proceed any further, I would like to ensure that the accused is able to follow the proceedings in a language he understands. Mr. Seselj, can you follow the proceedings in a language you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the time being, everything is all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Seselj, and good morning to you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. For the Prosecution, Mr. Dan Saxon, and my name is Mrs. Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I also recognise the presence of the standby counsel. Could you confirm that please for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN DER SPOEL
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. van der Spoel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and good morning to you, too. And I recognise also the presence of the accused who is defending himself. The last Status Conference was held on the 17th of February of this year. Today's Status Conference has been convened and is being held pursuant to Rule 65 bis, which requires a Status Conference to be convened every 120 days. The purpose of convening and holding a Status Conference is according to the same Rule 65 bis to organise exchanges between the parties so as to ensure expeditious preparation for trial; secondly, to review the status of the accused's case; and thirdly, to allow the accused the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto including his mental and physical condition. Before we proceed any further, the Trial Chamber wants to make it clear from the very outset that it has no intention to allow either of the parties to go beyond these limits set out by Rule 65 bis, and advises you that it will take the necessary steps to ensure that these proceedings are not abused of or derailed. I will proceed with the first item on today's agenda, which is, as usual in practically all the other Status Conferences in other cases, relates to issues of disclosure. You are aware that there are various types of disclosure that are dealt with under our Rules, and I am going to proceed by dealing with each one of these separately, starting first with the general disclosure which is dealt with by the Rules under Rule 66. You will recall that in the previous Status Conference of February 17, the Prosecution indicated that Rule 66(A)(ii) disclosure had not been completed because the Prosecution had sought nondisclosure of some witness statements in the motion of September 10, 2003, and were waiting for the Trial Chamber's decision. As you can refer to page 125 of the transcript. The Trial Chamber issued its decision on 11 February 2004. The decision was served upon the accused on the 17th of February. That is the same day in which the last Status Conference was held. The accused stated in the previous Status Conference that in the short time that he had available, he had read the decision and had no particular remarks to make, although he did make some submissions on his concept of defence in the light of the fact that he's defending himself. The accused was informed in the course of the last Status Conference that he had the right to appeal the decision within the appropriate time limit. Basically, and this is just to refresh everybody's memory, the decision of February the 11th, 2004, grants the request for the issuance of nondisclosure under Rule 53(A) and orders the Prosecution to provide more information to enable the Trial Chamber to determine the request for pre-trial protective measures. In response to the Trial Chamber's decision which I have just referred to, namely, that of the 11th of February, the Prosecution on the 23rd of April filed a so-called "Prosecution's submission of additional information concerning protective measures for vulnerable witnesses," confidential and partially ex parte. This is the way this motion or submission was filed. The submission further provides general background information relating to what according to the Prosecution were the, or are the dangers involved in the present case according to the Prosecution due to the behaviour of the accused, and furthermore the same submissions provide more detailed information in relation to specific witnesses for whom protective measures are sought. The Trial Chamber is in the course of weighing and reviewing this motion. It is assessing the Prosecution's request for protective measures in more detail. It is aware that this document was served upon the accused already and is not aware of any additional responses or comments from the accused in regard. In other words, the position is that we are still in the process of preparing a decision. This is a decision which is -- will be in all probability taken collectively, myself and Judge Antonetti and Judge Parker. But before I close the discussion on this particular matter, I would like to know if there are any other issues that either the Prosecution or Mr. Seselj would like to address in relation and only in relation to - for the time being we'll deal with other disclosures - in relation to disclosure contemplated by Rule 66(A)(ii).

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's nothing to add to your summary. It's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not want to file a response to that motion of the Prosecution in order to enable the Trial Chamber to make its decision as early as possible, reckoning that the Trial Chamber will act in accordance with the Rules of Procedure. The OTP has no reason to assume that I could disclose documents that are explicitly described as not public or that I could disclose names of protected witnesses. At the last Status Conference I said that I had no intention of doing so. Until the Prosecution finds evidence that I intend to disclose names of protected witnesses or nonpublic material, they do not have the right to machinations of this kind. That is why I ask that the Prosecution, in fact, the Trial Chamber make a decision as soon as possible in accordance with the Rules of the Procedure. It is clear that the OTP is not trial-ready. They have no evidence that would enable them to try this case. And that is why they're trying to delay in every way possible. That is why I do not intend to file a written submission because any written submission would increase this delay. In responding to my submission concerning the indictment, the Trial Chamber acted consistently with the Rules of Procedure, and therefore I expect the Trial Chamber to do so in this case as well. Awaiting this Status Conference, I learned that new amendments have been made to the Rules of Procedure and Evidence between the two Status Conferences, and to this day I have not been informed of the contents of these amendments. I don't know what they are about. Therefore, I request that I be given these amendments as soon as possible. I am prepared to deal with them as soon as possible, that I need to have them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Seselj. Thank you for both comments. We have -- or rather, I have taken note that you have no desire of making further -- any further submissions on the matter that I touched upon earlier. And I can at this point therefore confirm that we shall be in a position to hand down our decision pretty soon on the protective measures issues as they emerge from the documents that I referred to earlier. I have also taken note of your remarks on the amendments that have been put in place to the Rules of Evidence and Procedure since February 2004. As you may or may not be aware, I am the chairman of the Rules committee, and I have had an active role in the enactment of these amendments. You will recall that in the course of the last Status Conference you had complained that you had not been given a copy of the Rules of Evidence and Procedure in your own language. I had taken steps immediately to rectify this position, and I'm informed that on the 19th of March 2004 you were provided with a copy in the Serbian language of the entire corpus of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Within the -- by the end of this week, I will make sure that you will get a copy of the amendments that have added to the Rules which I can assure you have absolutely no bearing at all on your case or on these particular procedures or any other procedures that may be taking place, one of them refers particularly to the conditions which should obtain -- which should obtain if the Tribunal is to entertain a request by the Prosecutor to have certain cases transferred from here to domestic jurisdictions. But again, you will receive a copy of the amendments in your own language by the end of the week. They are not long amendments, and they can be translated if they have not already been translated into your language. Does that satisfy you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that satisfies me now, but I hope that in the future there will be no delays of this kind in submitting or rather providing me with the Rules. But -- because I must be informed as of the date when these amendments are adopted. Three or four months have elapsed now, and I still do not know what these amendments provide for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The first amendment hasn't even come into force as yet. It has still got to be published. I signed it last week anyway. So -- but you will be kept informed. I will ensure that you will be kept informed. There is no chance, as I see it, of any further amendments before the end of July. So you don't need to worry. And if there are further amendments to the Rules as probably there will be, you will be -- they will be translated, and as soon as they are translated you will be served with a copy of it. We move to Rule 67 material disclosure. Again, pardon me if I try to refresh everybody's memory, but this makes then it easier for us to progress on the particular issues that we are discussing. In the course of the last Status Conference, the Prosecution informed -- or the Trial Chamber informed the Pre-Trial Judge and acknowledged receiving from the accused a document of 80 pages -- well, actually it transpired later on that it was 294 pages and not 80 pages in B/C/S, under Rule 67(A)(i)(b) of the Rules. Just for the record, I might as well tell you what Rule 67 -- this part of Rule 67 is. This is -- provides that within a time limit set by the Pre-Trial Judge or by Chambers, the Defence shall notify the Prosecutor of its intent to offer any special defence, including that of diminished or lack of mental ability, et cetera, et cetera. Although the Rule in reality mentions the Defence or uses the words "the Defence shall notify the Prosecutor of its intent to offer a special defence," I signified my wish to have a courtesy copy of this document which I was eventually given. Sometime later, the Prosecution filed its second report concerning disclosure mentioning that it was reviewing the accused's document that I have just mentioned with a view to determining the factual and legal issues that are in dispute. The reason as put forward by the Prosecution was that it will then help it to produce a list of exhibits and begin disclosure of exhibits for trial pursuant to Rule 66(B). According to the Prosecution, this process would also help it to produce its final pre-trial brief. This is the last I heard from the Prosecution in regard to this exercise, that way back in February they had declared -- they had embarked upon. I would like now a formal update of the position from their point of view regarding the review of this document and the preparation of the lists of exhibits for purposes of disclosure and arrest. Please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document that we received from Mr. Seselj was a very helpful document. We have reviewed it meanwhile, and we actually found that there are -- there is room for agreement on facts that are not in dispute, and therefore we have sent a letter to Mr. Seselj in which we made proposals, actually four very substantial proposals for agreement on facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When did you send this letter?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We sent this letter on the 28th of May. And if you like, Your Honour, we can provide it to the Court as well. We have here copies of the letter where you can see that we have made four proposals, very substantial proposals for agreement. We have not yet received an answer by Mr. Seselj, but I assume he will answer to this letter. But I assume he will have to consider it carefully. Would Your Honour like to have a copy? We can provide it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think that would be useful to have.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. My apologies to the interpreters. Please do draw my attention. I usually switch it off between -- when I'm not speaking to allow -- to not disturb the transmission as much as I can. 6 Yes, but beyond this matter, this particular matter, namely, the proposal to the Prosecution to identify facts and matters which are not in dispute, what else have you done?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We have actually already a draft of the pre-trial brief that we intend to file, and we also have now a draft of the witness list and a draft of the exhibits list. But it's not in the final stage, and we therefore cannot disclose it. But what we can say so far is that we have on our witness list as of today 63 witnesses who will come to testify live, and 40 92 bis witnesses who will primarily speak about crime base. We have on our exhibits list currently about 900 exhibits, but it will be many more, and it will be heavily -- heavily populated with newspaper articles and interviews and statements that the -- Mr. Seselj did during the relevant time. That's a huge amount of exhibits on the witness list, and of course exhumation reports, reports of officers' orders, military orders and the like. But we are not at the moment in a position to disclose all this because it's not in the final stage. We think that by the end of the year, we will file our 65 ter submissions, if the Court allows us to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I would like to comment upon the statement of the representative of the Prosecution to the effect that they have three witnesses by now which would -- who would testify live. And 40 92 bis witnesses, which means that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think part of the interpretation must have arrived wrong to you or part of what you are saying is not being interpreted right to me. I heard you say "three witnesses," live witnesses. The Prosecution said 66 live witnesses, not three witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, 63.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, I misheard because I heard three. In that case, no comment. But I do have another comment on what the Prosecutor said concerning the 92 bis rule, namely, that they are preparing 40 witnesses who will be deposed, who will not appear directly in front of the Court. I can tell you in advance that I will contest every such deposition, every such statement. In case I am not able to cross-examine the witness directly, even if it concerns only crime base and these witnesses do not incriminate me directly. So that you don't waste your time, and I believe the Court will not be able to accept any such testimony a priori without my cross-examination. Whether it concerns 92 bis witnesses or transcripts from other cases because I have studied all the judgements that were available to me and I realise that Defence counsel did not try to challenge witness testimony regarding general circumstances, regarding the crime base, and not their clients in particular. Because I intend to challenge even such general Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. circumstances. I received this submission of the Prosecution on the 28th of May wherein the Prosecution suggests four agreed facts. I was not able to address the Prosecution in writing on this issue because as you know for more than six months now I have not been able to have any contact with my legal counsel. And it would be natural, you will agree, for me to contact my legal counsel before making a decision on such an important issue. I have been deprived of all contact with counsel and family alike. I was unable to address the Trial Chamber, too, because the Trial Chamber decided against my request for photocopying facilities. Instead it was suggested that photocopying will be done for me. As you know, it is not the accepted practice in this Court. In this case, I cannot send a document to the Prosecution because I have given it up for photocopying without having it in front of me. So I am forced to write in hand. I am prepared to state my view on those four points that are suggested by the Prosecution for agreement as stipulated facts, and if there is no objection on your part I can state my position now. I will try to speak more slowly than is my habit. (Redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's stop it, because this is going to take a long time, and the proper way to go about it, Mr. Seselj, is not to deal with it here but to consult your counsel. You are not correct in your assertion that you are being prohibited from communicating with your legal counsel. You are fully aware that the restrictions that you have in place at the Detention Unit do not apply to communications between you and your legal counsel as well as diplomatic and consular representatives. So what I suggest is that you try to formulate your position. I think you also need to consult your counsel, your advisors, on these matters. And I am also stopping you now for your own benefit. I don't want you to jump into making statements that can be used against you later on, Mr. Seselj. So take my advice. Go through this document carefully and take your time, discuss it with your advisors, and put down in writing what your position is with regard to each one of these four points. In the meantime, you can have all the time you need for this. I am not going to put a time limit. But the sooner you respond to the Prosecution, the better it is. I also am duty-bound to advise you further that you are not bound to respond to this document. In other words, you have a right to remain silent, here in the courtroom and from your cell in the Detention Unit. In other words, the fact that you have received this does not put an obligation on you to respond. So do take advice before we proceed any further on this matter. I -- this is the first time I'm seeing these documents. I see that the points that are being suggested to you to agree upon touch the core of the case that is being brought forward by the Prosecution. And I think my experience prompts me to terminate the debate on this matter now and give you the opportunity to measure your words and decide whether to respond to this document in the first place in the quiet of your cell, and after having taken proper advice from your advisors, the people you trust. Yes, any further comments on Rule 67 disclosure? Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm afraid that you have not been informed properly about these restrictive measures that have been imposed against me for more than six months. In the decision, which is unlawful, it says that I have the right to contact my legal advisors. But they do not recognise that I have any legal advisors. Maja Gojkovic and Slavko Jerkovic are my chosen legal advisors, but they did not acknowledge them. So I have the result to consult them but they have not been registered. So when I try to call these people through the prison guards and the special telephone that is for that purpose, the guards turn me down. You see, this is a game that makes it impossible for me to prepare my Defence. Your Honour, I appreciate your good intentions and your concern. You don't want me to do anything that will aggravate my position, but believe me I'm a man who thinks right and I can act immediately. Even today, I can state my views to the Prosecution in three sentences with regard to the counts leveled against me. Believe me, these will things I will never give up on any time in my life. They are the meaning of my life itself, and I would be the scum of the earth if I would give up on what I have lived for during these first 50 years of my life and these are the things that I'm going to live by for the rest of my life. So may I please state my position now and in that way the Prosecution will also receive --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, Mr. Seselj, I'm not going to allow you to proceed any further. Just -- I will reserve for you the position as I stated to you, and then you put your points in writing after having thought about it. But these are matters which should not be discussed at the Pre-Trial Status Conferences. Let's move -- and next time, please, Prosecutor, Madam Prosecutor, I would like to be informed of these exchanges promptly, not...

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I also want to exhort you, Madam Prosecutor, to do -- you mentioned the end of the year being able to present the 65 ter documents. May I suggest that you try and bring the date as forward as you can. I know that we are in June, but considering that we're talking only of 63 live witnesses and 42 92 bis, according to you, witnesses, I think you can do better. So I trust that you will do your utmost and report to me as the Pre-Trial Judge in the next Status Conference saying that you have terminated this exercise.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, just to mention, the amount of exhibits will be enormous, in particular when this letter that we proposed -- the four points that we proposed to Mr. Seselj, you will see it's -- when we know the answer to this, the exhibits could be very few. But if it is disputed what is in here, the written evidence, the documents, will be enormous. We have meanwhile actually tasked several experts dealing with these matters, and that's why we need time. It's not so much the witnesses; it's the exhibits that will need lot of time. Most of the exhibits that we are dealing with are actually in the Serbian language, and a huge amount of translation is needed. But of course, we will report to you on the next Status Conference. It's the exhibits, just to make sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I never ask for the impossible, but I ask for the optimum. And I do read -- this is why it's unfortunate that I have this document today. I do read what you have in mind here, and had I read it before I wouldn't even have allowed the accused to start answering. This is why I am concerned. The accused is not a lawyer. You are not a lawyer by profession, Mr. Seselj, and this is why I'm telling you be careful before you open your mouth on this. So with regard to Rule 92 bis, it doesn't mean -- I just need to explain to you one thing. Not every request put forward by the Prosecution for the production of evidence under the Rule 92 bis is accepted by the Trial Chamber. I have turned down many such requests and allowed others, depending, of course, most of the time also taking into consideration the position taken by the Defence. So you don't need to worry about the Rule 92 bis for the time being. These are pleasures yet to come, and we will deal with such requests when they reach the Trial Chamber. I cannot pronounce myself any further on the merits of such testimonies because I don't even know who these witnesses are or will be. Rule 68 material, let me go through my records first and point out what I have, and then correct me if I'm wrong. You are aware as I told you last time that Rule 68 has undergone some changes between the first of the Status Conferences and the last Status Conference. And it may undergo some further changes later on in July, which will not affect -- I don't know. I don't think it will affect these proceedings in any case for the time being at least. The first batch of Rule 68 material was disclosed at the Status Conference of the 3rd of July 2003, and that was under the old regime. And then a second set of material was disclosed in the course of the Status Conference of the 29th of October of last year. I take it that the accused acknowledged receipt of these documents. I now refer to you the Prosecution's second report on disclosure, which I mentioned to you earlier. You will recall also that in the course of the last Status Conference I pointed out that in that second report, the Prosecution discussed or tried to discuss or engage the Pre-Trial Judge in discussion on the recent amendments to Rule 68 and the implications for Rule 68 disclosures, in this case, as they were being envisaged or seen by the Prosecution. The Prosecution had explained on that occasion how it understands the Rule as amended; and following some discussion in the course of the last Status Conference, I had made it clear that it was not my intention or the intention of the Trial Chamber, Pre-Trial Chamber, to become involved or comment on the Prosecution's interpretation of the new Rule 68. I had made it clear that the reason for my position was that in my mind, Rule 68 as it was and as it is now is clear enough not to require any interpretation. The system of law which I am used to which draws from both common-law and civil-law traditions acknowledges that you speak of interpretation only when the law is unclear and requires interpretation; otherwise, you apply the law as it is. There are, however, certain issues that arose in the wake of the discussions on Rule 68 that I am going to discuss. I'm going to discuss them because I want to be updated basically. With respect to disclosure in electronic format envisaged in Rule 68(B) as amended, I recall that the accused reiterated that he will refuse to receive disclosure of documents which way of computer diskettes or contained in computer diskettes and that he will only accept paper documents. At the time, I had cut the discussion on this issue short knowing or being informed by the Prosecution that the process of disclosure of material under Rule 68(B) was by no means ready and also being aware that even the software was not available at the time. And I had declared that the issue of disclosure of such material falling under Rule 68(B) in electronic format will be deferred to future Status Conferences and as the matter arises. In the meantime, pretty soon after the last Status Conference, namely, on the 26th of March 2004, the accused filed his motion number 30 in which he requested a substantial amount of material from the Registry. Most issues in this motion have already been or are being addressed by the Registrar as I am informed. There is, however, one important issue that the Chamber has decided is an issue that needs to be addressed by the parties and subsequently by the Chamber. I am referring to the specific request made by the accused to have access to statements of all witnesses in all cases who mentioned his name in any context during testimonies before the Prosecutor or during testimonies before a Trial Chamber. I'm quoting his words because testimonies before the Prosecutor are better translated into statements made to investigators and to the Prosecutor. Following up on the Chamber's request which was notified to both parties, the Prosecution filed a response to the accused's motion on the 13th of April of this year. In its response, or in her response, I apologise, the Prosecutor as such - correct me if I am wrong, Madam - agrees that the accused should be provided access to such documents, but also touched upon a couple of important issues such as the need for protective measures for certain witnesses, the question of how to disclose this material electronically or in paper, and the question in which language this material should be disclosed. And I would like you now to update the Trial Chamber because you have presented the Trial Chamber with these problems without offering a solution, and I take it that a discussion on these issues will enable the Trial Chamber to finalise its motion which it has already started working upon from a general point of view, taking a deposition into consideration the position taken by both parties. I will first touch on the first issue that you raise; namely, that in not objecting, as I read you, to the Defence -- to the accused's request, you still want coverage when it comes to protective measures regarding certain witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but again, that is a very general observation. The Trial Chamber is not in a position to come to a conclusion not knowing who are these witnesses and what kind of protective measures you need to put in place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution understands that. However, before the Prosecution endeavours to embark on what will be a very large exercise, the Prosecution has stated its position on all these issues and asks that the Chamber make a decision that would obviously also include or incorporate the accused's willingness to receive materials in electronic format which would greatly expedite the amount of work involved in this exercise. So we were waiting for the accused to state his position on these matters in response to the Prosecution's motion and to hear from the Trial Chamber as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I don't think that is a logical approach. I think we need, Mr. Saxon, to approach it in a different fashion. My first question is, have you terminated the exercise of identifying all the documents that the accused may be referring to in his motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have done a preliminary search, and we have identified approximately 1.000 documents that would fall within the scope of the accused's request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right. That's number one. Please follow me with all the points because we will need to address this matter in an optimum fashion. Number two, have you decided in your mind whether to consent to the disclosure of all these documents in their entirety or only in the relevant parts which refer to the accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: As we explained in our response, Your Honour, the Prosecution submits that the proper way forward would be where we have sensitive witnesses who have either concerns about the nature of their testimony, for example, a sexual assault victim, or witnesses who have security concerns, we would submit that it would be sufficient to disclose only the portion or portions of the witness statement that refers to Dr. Seselj, the accused in this case. For other kinds of witness statements where those sensitive issues do not exist, the Prosecution would be willing to disclose the entire statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But have you identified the -- who these sensitive witnesses or witnesses that ought to be protected or statements that ought to be redacted are? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we have not undertaken that exercise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How many time do you require to do this exercise? Because I'm not going to allow you go through this exercise indefinitely. I know it's a laborious exercise, but if need be get an extra person allocated to the team who will dedicate his or her time to this exercise because we need to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, your suggestion to get an extra person allocated to the team is a decision made well above my pay grade --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know that, but I am telling you not for you to implement it but to pass on the message.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That message will be passed on, Your Honour. Your Honour, the trial team at a minimum would need two months to review all of these statements and carefully redact any sensitive materials from them that needs to be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then the other question, and remind that as soon as I have covered these points then we have to also decide how this is going to be referred back to the accused for his comments before we take a stand and reach a decision. The second is -- the question of how to disclose this material, electronically or in paper. This is only part of the wider question of disclosure in electronic format or in paper. But for the time being, I'm only interested in these documents that the accused has asked for and which you seem to consent to provide with the usual caveats that you have mentioned earlier. Have you taken a decision on how this disclosure will take place, whether it will take place in electronic format or in paper?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution's submission is that the disclosure should take place in electronic format. You will note that Rule 66(B) does not specify any particular form in which material -- in which access should be provided to the accused. And the Prosecution's submission is that the Prosecution should be able to provide that access in the form that is most efficient, not only to the Prosecution but to the entire Tribunal, Your Honour, and that includes this accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I have heard what you had to say. The position is being reserved on this matter after hearing the accused and also after being able to gauge the extent of labour and efforts that such an exercise would entail. Then there is also the question of language, and the question is in which language this material should be disclosed. When it comes to transcripts, I am fully aware that the transcripts exist only in English and in French. When it comes to statements given to the Prosecutor or to investigators of the Prosecutor or to others, I would imagine that there are copies, and sometimes the originals are also in B/C/S. So putting this in one basket, what is your position?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may just interject for a moment, the vast majority of witness statements given to the Prosecution are done in English. So the vast majority of the witness statements that we're talking about here would be, at least in their original version, in the English language. However, in the course of trial preparation, both for this case and for other cases as well, certainly at least a portion of these statements, witness statements, would already have been translated into the language that the accused understands. And so of course, if the Prosecution is ordered to make this material available to the accused, wherever we have a witness statement already in the Serbian language, we will provide that statement or the relevant portion of that statement to the accused in his language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: For other materials, Your Honour, we would submit that we would fulfil our obligation under the Rule by providing the statement in the English language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So basically, the position as I read it now is as follows -- rather, before I address you any further, I covered the three points that I needed to cover. Mr. Seselj, I address you now. You have heard what the Prosecution has stated. I will certainly provide within a few minutes by giving directives to the Prosecution on how to go about on some of these matters so you are put in a position in which you can then respond to their points and to their proposals adequately. But in the meantime, I would like you to tell me what your position is having heard now for the time being, having heard what the Prosecutor has stated. And take them one by one. With regard to the identification of sensitive witnesses and statements of witnesses that need to be protected, what is your position?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I guarantee that you will fully abide by the Rules related to witness protection, that I am not going to disclose a single name or single testimony that is protected, and that in this way I will not bring into question the integrity of the witness in any way. Until I break this promise and this guarantee, the Prosecution has no reason to doubt that I will indeed do so. Secondly, I think that the Prosecution should provide me with comprehensive documents, not only those sections that the Prosecution believes pertain to me because perhaps in another part of a testimony there is something that could be important evidence for me in Court proceedings, something that would bring into question some of the incriminations involved. Therefore, it is indispensable to have comprehensive documents. Secondly, it is impossible for the Prosecution to provide me with documents in electronic form, on diskettes, because I have the opportunity of using only documents that are on paper. A document on paper is a basic document. Anything else is mere possession, and not a single Court of law in the world can force an accused person to receive documents in any other form but in paper. I do not have a computer. I do not know how to use a computer, and I insist on receiving documents on paper. And finally, all required documents have to be in the Serbian language because I understand only the Serbian language and not a single other language. And nobody can force me to use any other language. That is what I have to state with regard to that particular question. That is item 3 of my request. But Your Honour, I would have some comments with regard to the other four points. Should I present them straight away or later?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which four points?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked the Registry to submit all judgements passed to date to me. I asked for that several times, but they have been providing me only in succession. However, there are a few judgements that are missing. The Kupreskic appeals judgement, they say they don't have it in the Serbian language, only in French and English. Then also the appeals judgement of Krnojelac, again they don't have it in the Serb language. Then the Obrenovic judgement, again they don't have it in the Serbian language. Some of these judgements were passed several years, like the Kupreskic judgement, I think it's been at least two years or perhaps even longer than that. I insist that this be submitted to me as soon as possible in the Serbian language because I am thoroughly studying the jurisprudence of this Court and I am making every effort to do so. Also, I asked for other judgements to be submitted to me after the 20th of January when I submitted this submission because, Your Honour, although I submitted this on the 27th of January they have answered me only just before the Status Conference itself, not when they can do it and when they're supposed to do it earlier on. They know I'm going to raise this at a Status Conference, so then they hurry only before Status Conferences. Then I also insisted because there are financial problems involved, I asked the Registry to provide me with information about all the expenses paid for the Defence of indictees before this Tribunal. My legal advisors submitted a bill amounting to 200.000 US dollars to me for the past year. I don't have the money to pay for that. I am going to get this in detail, but I handed this over to the Registry only a few days ago, this request put forth by my legal advisor. Also, I asked for all motions to be submitted to me in the Serbian language, all of those provided -- filed by Defence counsel and Prosecution responses to motions, and also Trial Chamber rulings with regard to these motions. Because you see, in all rulings of the Trial Chamber, reference is made to jurisprudence. I have to be familiar with specific jurisprudence. The Registry has rejected this. They did not provide me with the entire jurisprudence. They say that I should specify what I want, and then they're going to provide me with that. You, Your Honour, for example provided me with a valuable document, that is to say, the Brdjanin document that I requested. But I need so many documents because I have to know what I will use for different questions. This is a vast material, but if I am prepared to study this vast material, then it is the duty of the Registry to provide it to me. It is my affair whether I'm going to have enough time to study all of this. Sometimes I work 24 hours a day; sometimes I work even 25 hours a day if I get up an hour early. But my position is that I have to be familiarised with all jurisprudence, all decisions, motions, responses to motions, everything. I have one more point. I asked for all appeals to be provided to me, all of those that were filed so far. And also all the judgements, the appeals on judgements to be provided to me, and also the relevant judgements. I have to know because I am preparing myself for the appeal, and I will point out things that were not decided on properly in some other cases because the Defence did not argue some points that were proffered to them as agreed facts because many lawyers only worked on defending their own client without challenging the general political context and legal context. However, for my case, the most important thing is to challenge the general political and historical context because the Prosecution is not indicting me only with regard to specific crimes, but basically in terms of this general context, as you also put it. I received from the Registry a letter saying that they're giving me a comprehensive report on the work of the International Criminal Tribunal and also the policy of the Registry of paying Defence counsel. I got only one of those two documents, not both. And they claim that they sent me both. And on the receipt I wrote that one of these documents is missing. The other day, the guard wanted to give me a document in the English language, but I did not want to receive it. I don't speak this English language. I don't know this English language, and I'm never going to use it, to learn it, and it's my only private affair. In any case the most important thing is I have available to me in the Serbian language complete legal jurisprudence of this Tribunal. Without that, my defence would be impossible. If it's a question of room, the warden of the Detention Unit has the possibility to accommodate me. There is a room available where all this material can be stored. This should not be a problem for the warden. And if you intervene, he will do so. Because so far I have not even received the bookshelf that the previous Pre-Trial Judge decided somewhere in June or July last year should be given me. Concerning legal counsel, I have to draw your attention again, nobody is dealing with this issue, although at the last Status Conference you ordered that the Registry be provided with a transcript so that this issue is resolved. My legal counsel have not been registered. The Detention Unit treats them as nonexistent, and I have no contact with them. And in the latest decisions concerning restrictions, they tell me I should deal with that with the help of my legal counsel. How am I supposed to do that if I have contact with none? Another point, Your Honour, last time you did not allow me to raise the issue of my standby counsel. Under the ruling of the Trial Chamber of the 9th of May, 2003, standby counsel should be fluent in Serbian. Whereas Mr. van der Spoel has no clue about the Serbian language. Nobody, however, is raising the issue how the secretariat was allowed to violate this decision. When they are concerned, anything goes. And when I am concerned, unlawful restrictions are applied. That's what I had to say concerning my motion, my request. I insist that everything that is available in this Court as a document be made available to me on paper, judgements, appeals judgements, motions, submissions, decisions, orders, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Seselj. The position is as I explained it in the decision which followed your motion to which I referred to earlier. There are different compartments. There is the compartment which belongs to the Registrar and the Judge will not interfere in that compartment unless your rights, procedural rights, are being violated. Then there are other compartments which belong exclusively to the Pre-Trial Judge and the Pre-Trial Chamber and later on to the Trial Chamber in which the Registrar cannot interfere. The position is that you asked for certain matters which you consider important for you to have which we have absolutely no jurisdiction upon. The jurisdiction belongs exclusively to the Registrar. I think I made that clear in the decision and the directive that I handed down earlier on. And I will only intervene if there are -- there is inconsistency in the practice of the Registrar or if there is a violation. I have taken note of what you've said, namely that you're still missing some judgements, namely Kupreskic, Krnojelac and Obrenovic. I will inquire into this. Of course I cannot order the Registrar to give them to you, but if you are eventually not given these copies, please do let me know. Other matters which are the exclusive jurisdiction of the Registrar I will not interfere with until I am seized of the matter properly by means of a motion indicating why the Pre-Trial Chamber should intervene. That's the first thing. With regard to -- you mentioned again the question of language. I want you to know that I am very sensitive about your concern on this matter also because I give a lot of importance to the principle that the accused should always be in a position to follow the proceedings, and proceedings does not mean only court proceedings, but also documentary evidence and all that, in a language that he can understand. There are some problems that could arise mainly in view of how some of the articles, including Rule 68 disclosure, material disclosure, is regulated under our Rules. I am quite sure that I did explain to you during one, probably more, previous conferences, that Rule 68 material, on the face of it at least, does not require the Prosecution to disclose the material in your own language. I am also aware that the Prosecution did enter a statement that in spite of this they will do their level best to accommodate you when it comes to this. But I had made myself clear that since this is a matter that attaches to a pretended right, I will not pronounce myself any further until I am properly seized of the matter by means of motion. You may, and I'm telling you this because again you are not a lawyer and you may think you have done one thing while in actual fact you may not have done it the way you think. When you filed your motion number 30 in which you had asked for the disclosure of all the testimonies, statements of witnesses or persons that had mentioned you in the testimony or in the statement, you were not actually filing a motion referring necessarily to Rule 68 material. And this is where the problem is. If you are -- not interested, but if you want to proceed with your claim to have all documents, all material disclosed to you, and disclosed to you in your own language, including Rule 68 material, you have to file a proper motion, or at least make a declaration now. Then I will ask the Prosecution and give it time to respond to your request and will decide on your request in due course as necessary. But you need to make or file a proper motion, either in writing or orally, regarding specifically Rule 68 material because you haven't done so so far. You have stated that you want this and you want that and you want this and you want that, but there is no specific motion. And the Trial Chamber, Pre-Trial Chambers cannot actually state that it is seized of the matter. Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I did not file a motion under 68. My motion concerns jurisprudence. And item 3 regards a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. specific part of past jurisprudence. It does not have to be exculpatory material under Rule 68. It can also be Prosecution material; it can also be neutral to my legal status, my legal position. But I wish in the course of my preparation to become acquainted with that material. All this, therefore, concerns jurisprudence. And as far as I understand your Rules, it is the Registry who is in charge primarily, and they are supposed to give it to me. As for Rule 68, the Prosecution has disclosed a lot of exculpatory material to me so far. So many documents, exculpatory documents concerning the Ovcara case that I am even expecting them to abandon this part of the indictment, so convincing I find this material. Also material concerning Western Slavonia, Zvornik, Samac, et cetera. But they have been insisting to delivering this material to me in the form of floppy disks and CDs, and I refused that whereupon they provided it to me in paper. I am making no further problem. And I expect them to disclose all the exculpatory material to me soon. Now, concerning jurisprudence, I must be absolutely familiar with all the past jurisprudence and I must be able to follow all the current proceedings because jurisprudence is being enriched as we speak every day. There is not a single court or Tribunal in the world whose jurisprudence could be an alternative to me. For instance, you cannot say that the jurisprudence of another Tribunal could replace the jurisprudence of this one. I need to know the jurisprudence of the ICTY. I therefore ask you to address the Registry, which is after all an administrative unit, because they are thwarting my efforts to familiarise myself with the jurisprudence. I have raised this issue today at the Status Conference, but I can also file a written submission if you so wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I would prefer if you file a proper motion, Mr. Seselj, with your reasons included. Incidentally, I am just being provided with, because I was not aware of this as I said, the Registrar is not accountable to me for the exercise of what is strictly his domain like I am not accountable to the Registrar for what is strictly my own competence and jurisdiction. I am informed, and I can go through this list briefly with you. I am informed that the judgement in the case against the Samac, the Simic case, in other words, is available in B/C/S; same applies to Milomir Stakic; same applies to Momir Nikolic and Dragan Nikolic; and also, General Talic and Banovic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Galic, correction. General Galic, not Talic. Talic was not tried.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Galic, General Galic. It may have been a bad interpretation. And final judgement on Banovic, that these are all available in your own language and that you have been -- I just want to make sure that you have been given these copies.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have received all that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then there are three, as you said, judgements which are not yet available in your language, and that is the Kupreskic, the Krnojelac, and the Obrenovic judgements. They are being worked upon. And until they are available in your language, you obviously cannot have them. You'll need to wait until they are available, and I am informed that as soon as they are available in your own language they will be provided to you. With regard to the rest, as I said, the Registrar has the power and the jurisdiction and the competence to decide certain issues following requests that are made by the accused directly to him. The Trial Chamber does not interfere with these matters and with the discretion exercised by the Registrar unless cause is shown to the Chamber, in this case, the Pre-Trial Chamber, why it should interfere. I notice that the Registrar decided to accede to some of your requests and to reject some of your other requests. If you feel aggrieved now that you have the Rules of Evidence and Procedure in your own language as well, you know what the options are, and you have every right to seek a remedy according to those Rules. Until the Trial Chamber or whoever, because it need not necessarily be the Pre-Trial Chamber, it could be someone else, is properly seized of these matters, there is no further point in discussing them here in the course of the Status Conference. Of course, I did allow you to air your grievances because on the face of it they seem, or you present them as related and as pertinent to your problems in trying to defend yourself. And I will continue to do so. However, I am limited by the separate jurisdiction of the Registrar in which I do not interfere and will interfere only if I am shown cause properly by means of a motion that the Registrar is using his discretion in a way which is tantamount to depriving you from the right to have a fair trial and to prepare an adequate defence. So the position is reserved both with regard to disclosure in the language he understands, particularly under Rule 68. There's no question under Rule 66, the Rule is very specific. It says "in a language that the accused understands." Why those words are notoriously absent in Rule 68?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, with your permission in relation to the disclosure in the format we propose, in relation to the format of disclosure, electronic disclosure, of course we also have Defence counsels here that were not used to this form of disclosure, but there is the possibility to have assistance by a paralegal who could assist Mr. Seselj in reviewing electronic disclosure and searching documents and that is his possibility, to simply request a paralegal to assist him in this. So that should be not be a barrier. And in relation to disclosure in the English language, actually in relation to 66(B), it doesn't say it needs to be in English. But my main point I want to make is the Prosecution actually got the impression that Mr. Seselj is actually able to both to read and understand English and to speak English because we have here a CD with an interview that Mr. Seselj gave during the events to a Dutch TV station, and here he gets the questions in English language and answers in English language, very sensible answers in normal English. So we got the impression that he understands English, at least more than he claims here. And if Your Honour wants, we can play it here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You don't need to play it here for the time being, Madam. The -- I don't want to jump the gun. We are discussing issues that are arising, but of which the Trial Chamber, Pre-Trial Chamber is not yet properly seized with. When it comes to disclosure, you have the responsibility of disclosure. I will intervene only, and I will be seized only the moment you disclose material which the accused contests as not being disclosed according to the Rules. In other words, when it comes to question of language, I will intervene only when I am seized with the matter. In other words, because it could well be that you will disclose everything in a language that he understands; it may well be that he will satisfied with what you disclose. So I will not jump the gun. I will take things in the proper order. I appreciate what you have stated. But that comes into issue only if you are not bound to disclose a particular document in the Serbian language, and you disclose it in the English language and the accused comes forward and says that he did not understand the English language, that he wants it to be disclosed in his own language. Then there will be two issues: First, whether he has a right to have it disclosed in his language according to the specific rule which would be applicable, and secondly whether it is of prejudice to him if it is disclosed in the English language now that you are alleging that he is familiar with that language. I don't think we need to discuss this any further. But I am going to give you a time limit of two months to regulate yourself as a follow-up and in the wake, first, of Mr. Seselj's motion number 30, and also along the lines of the discussion that we have had until now, basically sensitive witnesses, witnesses that need to be protected, documents that you may ask to be redacted and so on and so forth. I want also to make one point clear, and this is to pre-empt any further discussion on the matter: There may be documents as I understand you which you would not like to disclose in total.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the position that has been taken by Mr. Seselj it seems is that he would prefer them or he would insist that they be provided in total because there may be other elements in them which may be relevant for him. Now, we are discussing a proper motion, motion number 30 in which he submitted a specific request. If there are any documents that you need to redact or if there are any documents which you believe should not be submitted in toto, you need to submit them to me, the Pre-Trial Judge in toto indicating what you would like to redact and indicating what you would not like to have disclosed to the accused, and it will be I who will decide whether there will be the redactions that you will request or whether there will be nondisclosure of the nonrelevant, according to you, material in the statements. I am making that position very clear as from now. In other words, before any such disclosure takes place, it will be under my authorisation if it is to be redacted and if it is to be disclosed not in its entirety. Have I made myself clear?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, that's understood, Your Honour. And otherwise we proceed as we have proposed in our submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, obviously. But you have two months within which to finalise this exercise. And I'm saying two months first because two months was indicated by your colleague, and also because two months is halfway between this Status Conference and the next. All right?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you for your cooperation. One moment, because I have... So basically, that covers all the points that I had mentioned. As soon as you have finalised this exercise, then we will proceed with our decision. I mean, on the points that are not controversial, more or less we are already prepared. So we will only need to concentrate on the other issues that I mentioned earlier. There are a few things that I want to make sure of. I was informed that -- I have been informed, rather, that you have been provided with the copies of the videotapes of the last two Status Conferences. Is that correct, Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have received these copies with some delay, though. But I do insist that these copies be submitted to me immediately after Status Conferences. Once the trial starts, I am afraid that if I do not get copies immediately, I will not be in a position to do my job properly. As far as I know, the technical facilities are here are such that I can get copies of everything that goes on while I'm still in the court building. This happened when the Special Prosecutor came and the investigator of the special court in Belgrade when they came to interview me in relation to the assassination of Zoran Djindjic, I got the cassettes straight away, immediately after that. May I mention to you in passing, Your Honour, that the Special Prosecutor is not going to prosecute me with regard to that particular case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. I just want to confirm that you have received them. When we request them ourselves, we have to wait. We don't receive them within the day, I can assure you, Mr. Seselj. I am also informed, and I just want to you intervene only if I am not connect. I am also informed that the Rules of Evidence and Procedure were handed to you in your language on the 19th of March. And as I said, you will receive the B/C/S version of the amendments as soon as possible. I'll endeavour to have them delivered to you by the end of the week as I promised you. I was informed last week, early last week, that the decision, the Brdjanin decision that I had given relating to Rule 68 had not been given to you as yet, but I then confirmed later on that in the course of last week it was handed to you. And I heard you confirm this because you referred to it earlier on. If there are any other decisions that you are aware of that you need from me, then I can provide you, of course, with them, with the help of the Registrar because obviously I do not keep them in stock myself.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot ask for a specific decision now. But in principle, I've asked for all decisions so that I would have them at hand when I need them so that I could study the jurisprudence of this Tribunal thoroughly because I'll have a few years to do that. As from what I heard, this trial of mine has planned for 2007. So I have ample time to study all of that. But I have to receive all of it in order to be able to study it. I cannot give you any specific details as to which particular document I would like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, I am not aware of such a date, Mr. Seselj. And very much, things very much depend on the progress that we register in these Status Conferences in the first place, which, as I explained in the beginning, should be limited only to the purposes which Rule 65 bis points out, and not beyond that. The moment things get complicated, I am afraid it won't serve you any good because it can only procrastinate the proceedings. On my part, I can promise you that I have absolutely no interest and no intention in delaying these proceedings. I will do my best to accelerate the process. And I will, as I told you in the very beginning, not allow either of you to transgress the boundaries or the parameters of the Status Conference and will establish deadlines for you if and when necessary so that the whole process can be accelerated. There's one thing obviously that you ought to be aware of. There are six trials ongoing at the moment, and for another trial to start one has to finish. And it is the policy of this Tribunal also to give priority to those cases which have arrived here before others, especially in those cases where the accused is still in detention like you are. As I stated in the beginning of the sitting, one further reason for holding these conferences is to review the status of the accused's case, and more or less what I have just stated covers the matter. I do appreciate that you are concerned that, especially if you have been told that your trial won't start before 2007, that this is a justified concern for you to have. But again, I appeal to you to be as cooperative with the Pre-Trial Chamber as much as you can, and with the rest of the Tribunal as much as you can because it's only in this environment that we can register progress in a way which would guarantee you in anticipation of the trial. Before I ask you to make any remarks on your health, et cetera, are there any other comments that you would like to make regarding any other issues that are related only to the case, the trial, and the preparation of the trial? Not any other matters, in other words. I mean, I will start with you. Do you have any further statements to make?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have one point. And it relates to the recent decision of the Trial Chamber on the motion of the accused's challenging jurisdiction and form of the indictment. We have actually -- we have the intention to amend paragraph 11 of the indictment, but as we have already on Friday filed a notice that we would appeal the Vojvodina aspect, that is, paragraph 12 of the indictment, we would ask permission to wait with the amendment of paragraph 11 as the appeal is still pending because otherwise we would have to amend twice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Has the appeal or the motion been filed?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, the motion has been filed on Friday, and you have received notice and alternatively request for certification in case the appeal is not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm going to make myself very clear on this. First of all, I think since -- I was not aware that you had filed a motion, I only was informed that a motion has been filed just before entering the courtroom. I was not aware that it was filed last Thursday or last Friday. And I am not blaming anyone for it; don't misunderstand me. We don't always get informed of a motion having been filed on the same day. Sometimes it's the day after; sometimes it's even two days later. Although you may have the idea of -- you may have formed the idea that this is something that -- in which Mr. Seselj may not have voice and a chapter, it's not correct. Because Mr. Seselj has an interest in not having you exercise a right of appeal if you don't have it. So the question is that I don't even know if he has been served with this motion. Perhaps you can answer that question first. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. The Prosecution filed a motion last Thursday or Friday. When did you file it?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Sorry. We gave it to the Registry on the Thursday, but because there needed to be the translation it was filed on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It was translated in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And do you know if it has served on the accused?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, have you received any documents from the Prosecution, end of last week or today, this morning? I mean, it's for that matter.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I received from the Prosecution earlier the document announcing appeal to the decision of the Trial Chamber II on my objection or challenge. I will not challenge this motion so as not to waste time because I believe your decision was right. And the Prosecution cannot prove an international armed conflict in Vojvodina or the warring parties. But I will object to the very appeal of the Prosecution. However, I did not receive this second document. I did not receive their request for amendment of the indictment. And I am surprised a little that they announce their intention to appeal and their intention to amend the indictment at the same time. I suppose they should first wait for the decision of the Trial Chamber on their appeal and then see if they're going to amend the indictment. If by virtue of announcing their intention to amend the indictment they renounce their appeal, I have nothing against it. But I still haven't received this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Then it's obviously what you have said; I can understand knowing that you are not a lawyer. And this is why you're not understanding exactly what the Prosecution is trying to do. The Prosecution obviously wants the -- wants to cover itself not knowing if their appeal, which they will file later on, will be rejected by the three Judges that according to the Rule have to decide whether it should even be considered, whether it's in accordance with the Rules. And the reason for doing so is that unless they cover themselves, they may find themselves in the situation where the three Judges appointed by the President will say this is not ritual, this is not according to procedure, you have no right to appeal the way you are appealing or on the ground that you are appealing, and then finding itself, being unable to file an appeal based on another ground or another different part of the Rules because the time limit would have lapsed and they wouldn't have asked for certification in the meantime. I think -- yes. Yes. How much time do the technicians require? We will soon be ready. But five minutes? What? We'll wait until they change the tape. And can we proceed and conclude after that? We have got only one item left on the agenda which shouldn't last long. But I want your okay. Okay? Okay. Thank you. So we'll have a short break of five minutes. We can stay in here, all of us. And when we have the signal that the tape -- a new tape has been placed, we can proceed. Thank you. So I thank you all. The position I was trying to explain, I'm going to be very blunt with you, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff. I was irritated a lot when I saw this motion. I'm not here to give you advice, and I will not give you advice. But I can tell you that the Trial Chamber cannot entertain this request of yours. There are other options that you have open. But I cannot accept a position where you have chosen one way of proceeding, and then you come forward and you tell me, but, I've chosen this one and not that one, because I think this is the right way to go. But if I am not successful, please can you intervene now before it will be too late to keep the other options open for me. No. I will not intervene as a Pre-Trial Judge. If you choose one way, you know of the Latin principle, selecta novia selecta una via non datum recursus ad altera. There is no one stopping you from pursuing also the other way, and there is no one -- I will not stop you from pursuing both way now if you want to. But I cannot especially -- I'm sure you cannot quote me a precedent, but I cannot at this point in time tell you, I will wait like you to see what the three Judges appointed by the President in appeal will decide. And then, if they decide in favour of you, it's okay, there is no point in discussing certification any further. If they decide against you saying that this was not the right way to appeal, then, okay, you will be safe, you will be able to proceed because I have kept the -- what should already be dead alive. So do make your choices. It seems that you have already made one choice. I think you may still be in time of making another choice as well. Then one of them will drop. But don't ask me to resort to this kind of approach because I will not approach it. So the decision is being handed down orally and is the Pre-Trial Chamber has -- the Pre-Trial Judge has taken note of your request and is hereby deciding that it will only be seized to decide on matters related to certification if there is a proper motion asking for certification. But the Pre-Trial Chamber has no authority as such to postpone or prolong the terms established by the Rules for the filing of a motion for certification simply on the pretext that has been put forward by the Prosecution. So on the basis of this, I think you should be able to know how to regulate yourself.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. We didn't expect any other decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm glad to hear that. I'm glad to hear that. So, Mr. Seselj, the Rule applicable that I read out in the beginning also makes it incumbent on me to ask -- to give you the opportunity to raise issues relating to the case including your mental and physical conditions. I appeal to you to be brief on this, be to the point, and not try to make a political issue out of it because I will stop you. I will want to know what complaints you have. Just mention the complaints, but don't try to make a political speech because I will stop you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm surprised by your cautioning because I never made political speeches here. I only represent my rights and my interests in this process. I have three purely status-related issues to raise. The first status-related issue is the following: Carla del Ponte, chief Prosecutor, on the 31st of January gave an interview to Croatian television, and she mentioned my name in this interview in a very negative context. Also, the spokesperson of the court and the spokesperson of the OTP mentioned my name in a negative context several times. On TV Sense [phoen] which is edited by The Hague Tribunal and produced by The Hague Tribunal, also after the last Status Conference they grossly misinterpreted the content of this Status Conference for political purposes. I'm not the one who is trying to politicise this Court. Others are trying to do this. Therefore, I insist that if the spokesperson of the OTP has the right to address the public, if the spokesperson of the Tribunal has the right to address the public, I insist that I be given this same right once a month a press conference regarding the state of the case. Furthermore, in a programme called The Hague Chronicle of TV Sense, this last Saturday on the 12th of June, terrible insults were levelled at the Serb people, the Serb national tradition --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you, Mr. Seselj. One question. I am going to stop you. Do you have any complaints with regard to, or any comments with regard to your health? Yes or no. If you have, please, identify them. And if you need to go into private session because of personal matters relating to health, we will go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have the right to point out three status-related problems, to raise three status-related issues, Your Honour. I did not politicalise this Status Conference at all in any way. Do you allow me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, I don't allow you, Mr. Seselj. I am the Presiding Judge, I am the Trial Judge, and you will do what I say. I am asking you whether you have any remarks to make to the Court on your state of health.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I have objections to the translation of the documents. Do you allow me to present that here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, with regard to the translation of documents, I certainly allow you to make submissions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once a month, I received from the Registry of the Tribunal the unlawful decision prohibiting me to communicate with my family and friends and even with my legal advisors. Twice it happened, on 9th of February and in the month of March, that in the version in the Serbian language the Registrar says that I am indicted for genocide. Check the documents. In the version in the English language, there is no mention of genocide. That is a very grave problem for me. And I don't think that I am politicising things in any way now. Furthermore, I looked at the transcripts of Status Conferences which were submitted to me in the English language. The content was changed of what I was saying, and even the word "Your Honour" was used. That's a word I never used. Because in my country it is a polite form of address and customary form of address to say Mr. Judge or Madam Judge, and that is the same thing that the Muslims and Croats do. And I cannot allow the interpreters to misinterpret my words in such a way. It is sufficiently polite in the Serbian language to say Mr. Judge, and that is the only way in which lawyers and the accused and prosecutors address the Court. Anything else would be different. Since you did not allow me to raise the problem of this total isolation that I have been submitted to last time, I have to raise it again. Mr. Judge, detention is a measure that is imposed so that the accused would not escape, would not destroy evidence with relation to the crime mentioned in the indictment, and also not to affect witnesses that would be involved. Those are the only three reasons why detention is imposed. Detention cannot be abused for preventing an accused to have his own private life. I have my own private life and I have my professional life. Why are both being rendered disabled? Why can I not function from detention in professional terms as I did function previously in my life? In this compilation of Registry documents, an unheard of politicisation is carried out. What it says here is that I am prohibited from any kind of contact because my political party is running in the elections, a candidate from my party is running in the presidential elections, Mr. Tomislav Nikolic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, stop, stop. There is an order in place. I have told you this before. There is an order in place by the Registrar ordered by the Deputy Registrar, sometimes, which restricts your communications with the outside world. You're not correct in stating that you are prohibited from your family. You can contact your family, but the order is that this -- your contact with your family will be subject to live monitoring under conditions prescribed by the commanding officer of the Detention Unit. I'm making myself clear. I do not have jurisdiction here and now to enter into the merits or the merits of these decisions which are taken by the Registrar or his deputies, and as they are implemented by the commander of the Detention Unit, commanding officer of the Detention Unit. If you are not happy with these orders and how they are being renewed on a monthly basis, you have a remedy. But the remedy is not to come here and complain. You have a remedy; you can file a proper appeal to whoever according to the Rule is authorised to deal with these matters. And let's stop the discussion here. It's not me who has authorised these restrictions. I cannot intervene in this matter because it's not my jurisdiction. It can be the jurisdiction of the President of this Tribunal if you seek redress from him. But until you seek redress from him, the position is what it is. You are no longer in the same position as you were before you surrendered yourself to this Tribunal. You are a detainee now. So that is the position. And let's bring it to an end. Are there any complaints that you would like to raise with regard to your state of health? And let's leave it at that. The rest you can take up with the persons who are empowered to deal with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course, it has nothing to do with the trial. And it also has nothing to do with me. There being no further complaints, I declare this Status Conference to end here. Thank you. And the next Status Conference will be convened within the 120-day limit which is provided by the Rule 65 bis. Thank you.
